# Coast

> Coast is a free iOS and Android app for fitness on autopilot: working adults, men and women, who want results with the least time. You set it up once, then it plans your training and your food. You set your goal weight and body fat; the app plans the order of cuts and bulks to get there (a "route" of trim and build phases) and how long each one takes, from published research. Then it builds weekly high-protein meal plans around your calories, mostly batch meals you cook once for 8 tubs, with every ingredient and step, one shopping list and one cook, plus a periodised training program with sets, reps, rest and deload weeks already set. Everything is built in the app in about a minute from research-backed rules; there is no AI inside the app. Free, no ads, no account, data stays on the phone.

Coast's library has 75 meals: 37 batch meals you cook once for 8 tubs (29 in the slow cooker, 8 oven bakes; 31 take 10 minutes or less of hands-on work; every one keeps 3 days in the fridge and freezes), 16 breakfasts, 10 desserts and 12 backup meals (smoothies for when a meal gets missed), every one photographed with exact ingredients and every step. Meals can be swapped and the day rebalances to the calorie and protein targets. Training programs run 1 to 6 days a week, at a gym, at home or bodyweight only, up to a year long, with 144 exercises. 25 decisions the app makes carry a confidence label (strong, good, best estimate) and link to 42 sources. Built in Canberra, Australia, by Ryan Novinc, who is using the app on himself in public: 77 kg at the July 2026 restart, 80.6 kg at 23.8% on the September DEXA, routed down to 72.9 kg at 16% and then up to 90 kg at 13%.

## Who this is for

Busy working adults, men and women, who want to eat right and train with the least time. Often people who already go to the gym but whose food is a mess. Goals cover losing weight, building muscle and both; gaining weight is one goal option, not the whole app.

## Core pages

- [Try it](https://getcoast.fit/try/): Build your plan in the browser, no sign-up: answer a few questions and see your route, your training program and your weekly meals, made by the same engines as the app.
- [Home](https://getcoast.fit/): What the app does, the route, the meals, the week, the training, the evidence and FAQ. Primary reference page.
- [Meals](https://getcoast.fit/meals.html): All 75 meals with calories, protein and hands-on time, filterable by batch meals, breakfast, desserts, backup meals, slow cooker, oven bakes, 10 minutes hands-on or less and 40 g+ protein.
- [Recipe pages](https://getcoast.fit/r/): One page per meal with ingredients, method, macros and how it keeps, e.g. https://getcoast.fit/r/butter_chicken_and_rice/butter_chicken_and_rice_tub/
- [Programs](https://getcoast.fit/programs/): Free periodised programs (beginner to advanced) that import directly into the app.
- [Exercises](https://getcoast.fit/exercises/): 144 exercises with start and finish photos, what each trains and how to do it.
- [6 hours a week](https://getcoast.fit/time/): How the figure of about 6 hours a week saved on food was worked out, from Australian time-use data, a food-logging study and the app's own meal plans.
- [How we know](https://getcoast.fit/research/): The 25 decisions the app makes, what the studies found, the confidence level and the sources, plus the full reference files.
- [The Lab](https://getcoast.fit/lab/): The founder's own route on the app, with DEXA scans, the planned route and progress photos as they happen.
- [Free cookbook](https://getcoast.fit/cookbook/free-cookbook): "The One Cook Cookbook: batch meals that cover your week", 86 pages: the 37 batch meals plus the breakfasts, desserts and backup meals as a printable PDF, free in exchange for an email.

## Guides

- [Blog](https://getcoast.fit/blog.html): Articles on training, nutrition, cutting and bulking, protein, training volume, rep ranges, deloads and rest periods, each with its sources.

## Get the app

- [Coast on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/au/app/json-fit/id6758357834): Free download. iOS.
- [Coast on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.RyanNovinc.JSON): Free download. Android.

## The 25 decisions the app makes (How we know)

Each with the confidence label the app shows (strong, good, or best estimate) and the lead source. Numbers in the titles are example values; the app computes yours. Full detail: https://getcoast.fit/research/

- [route] Lose about 0.5 to 1% of your weight a week — strong. Garthe et al. 2011
- [route] The faster pace needs fat to spare — estimate. Alpert 2005
- [route] Recomp keeps the deficit under 500 kcal — strong. Murphy & Koehler 2022
- [route] Ease in at about 0.5 to 1% a week — estimate. Vargas-Molina et al. 2026
- [route] For men, 10 to 15% body fat is the sweet spot — good. Frederick & Haselton 2007
- [route] Natural muscle tops out near an FFMI of 25 — estimate. Kouri et al. 1995
- [route] Build about 0.25 kg of muscle a week — estimate. Morton et al. 2018
- [route] Build up to 18%, trim back to 16% — estimate. Galgani et al. 2025
- [route] Women's plans stop at 22% body fat — estimate. Mursu et al. 2023
- [route] Expect some fat with the muscle — estimate. Garthe et al. 2013
- [route] Phases end on your weight, not a body-fat reading — good. Zemski et al. 2019
- [route] Decisions wait for a month of weigh-ins — estimate. Bull et al. 2019
- [training] 16 hard sets a week for each muscle — good. Pelland et al. 2026
- [training] Each muscle about twice a week — good. Schoenfeld, Ogborn & Krieger 2016
- [training] Most sets in the 5 to 15 rep range — good. Schoenfeld et al. 2017
- [training] Stop most sets a rep or three short of failure — good. Robinson et al. 2024
- [training] 2 to 3 min rests on the big lifts — good. Singer et al. 2024
- [training] A lighter week every 5 weeks — estimate. Bell et al. 2023
- [training] Your training stays the same while you cut — estimate. Roth et al. 2023
- [meals] 170 g of protein a day — good. Morton et al. 2018
- [meals] Eat 2,180 kcal, about 500 under maintenance — good. Murphy & Koehler 2022
- [meals] Never below 1,800 kcal — estimate. Loucks & Thuma 2003
- [meals] Maintenance of about 2,630 kcal — estimate. Mifflin et al. 1990
- [meals] Eat about 10% above maintenance — estimate. Garthe et al. 2013
- [meals] Macros worked out from weighed ingredients — good. Fukagawa et al. 2022

## Blog posts

- [Volume or Effort? What Actually Builds Muscle](https://getcoast.fit/blog/sets-or-effort.html) (2026-09-30): Volume is the dial and effort is what makes a set count. The research supports both camps because they're describing one rule from opposite ends.
- [5 to 30 Reps: The Range Is Wide, the Rule Is Narrow](https://getcoast.fit/blog/five-to-thirty-reps.html) (2026-09-23): Muscle grows anywhere from about 5 to 30 reps when sets are taken close to failure. The rep count is almost free. The effort isn't, and some exercises need high reps just to hit the right muscle.
- [You Need More Protein On a Cut](https://getcoast.fit/blog/more-protein-on-a-cut.html) (2026-09-16): 1.6 g per kilo is the number for building. In a deficit, protein's job changes from building to protecting, and the research says 2.2 to 3 g per kilo, higher the leaner you are.
- [Cut First or Bulk First? Same Finish Line](https://getcoast.fit/blog/cut-first-or-bulk-first.html) (2026-09-09): The partitioning argument is dead, the arithmetic says the order costs about two weeks either way, and the only real rule is to stay inside a healthy body-fat band.
- [Cutting Fast Doesn't Cost What You Think](https://getcoast.fit/blog/cutting-fast-versus-slow.html) (2026-09-02): A fast cut doesn't strip your muscle for good. It costs you the gains a slow cut leaves room for, and it costs you adherence. And the leaner you are, the slower you physically have to go.
- [Cutting Doesn't Change Your Training](https://getcoast.fit/blog/training-doesnt-change-with-your-diet.html) (2026-08-26): Weekly hard sets build muscle. Food decides your fat. The phase you're in should move where you sit inside each muscle's range, and nothing else.
- [Fasted Cardio Doesn't Burn More Fat](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-fasted-cardio-matters.html) (2026-07-29): Training on an empty stomach is sold as a fat-loss cheat code. Over a full day the difference disappears, and you may just be lifting worse for it.
- [You Can't Crunch Away Belly Fat](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-spot-reduction-matters.html) (2026-07-22): Targeted ab work to burn stomach fat is one of fitness's most stubborn myths. The research is clear: you don't get to choose where fat comes off.
- [You Don't Always Need to Squat Ass to Grass](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-squat-depth-matters.html) (2026-07-15): Full depth is treated as the only real squat. Depth does matter for some muscles, but the all-or-nothing framing misses what the evidence actually shows.
- [The Anabolic Window Is Hours, Not Minutes](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-protein-timing-matters.html) (2026-07-08): The post-workout protein scramble is sold as a 30-minute emergency. The research says the window is open for hours, and total daily protein is what counts.
- [You're Probably Eating More Protein Than You Need](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-protein-amount-matters.html) (2026-07-01): The "more is always better" mantra breaks down past a point. The useful ceiling sits lower than most lifters think, and the rest is just expensive.
- [Stretching Won't Save You From Injury](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-stretching-matters.html) (2026-06-24): Static stretching before training is sold as injury insurance. The evidence says it does little for injury risk and can blunt your strength. Here's what the research actually supports.
- [You Don't Need to Train to Failure](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-training-to-failure-matters.html) (2026-06-17): Going to absolute failure on every set feels hardcore, but the research shows it adds fatigue without adding much growth. Here's where stopping short actually wins.
- [We Didn't Make the AI Smarter. We Gave It the Answer Key](https://getcoast.fit/blog/ai-answer-key.html) (2026-06-10): Ask a general-purpose AI about fitness and it confidently repeats the field's oldest myths. Here's how Coast feeds it curated, citation-backed research so it applies the right knowledge instead of guessing.
- [Cardio Isn't Stealing Your Gains](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-cardio-matters.html) (2026-06-03): The interference effect is real, but "cardio kills gains" is a wild overstatement of it. Here's what the research actually says, and the three things that decide whether cardio costs you anything.
- [If You're Not Sore, It Still Worked](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-soreness-matters.html) (2026-05-27): Delayed-onset muscle soreness feels like proof your workout worked. The research says it's a signal of novelty, not growth, and chasing it can backfire.
- [Your Deload Is Probably Fake](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-deloads-matter.html) (2026-05-20): Most lifters either never deload or do a "fake" one that clears no fatigue. Here's what a real deload is, and the honest truth about how thin the evidence for it actually is.
- [The 8-12 Rep Range Isn't Magic](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-rep-ranges-matter.html) (2026-05-13): The hypertrophy rep range of 8 to 12 reps is one of the most cited rules in fitness. The research says it isn't biologically privileged. Here's what actually drives muscle growth.
- [Why Most Bulks Are Wrecked by Too Much Fiber](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-fiber-matters.html) (2026-05-06): The standard fiber recommendation scales with calories. For lifters eating 4,000+ kcal, that math gets ugly fast. Here's why bulking and cutting need different fiber strategies.
- [The 30g Protein Rule Is Mostly Made Up](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-protein-distribution-matters.html) (2026-04-29): You've heard you can only absorb 30 grams of protein per meal. The number is a practitioner extrapolation, not a proven threshold. Here's what the research actually says.
- [The 8-Hour Eating Window Isn't What You Think](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-meal-timing-matters.html) (2026-04-22): Time-restricted eating is sold as a magic bullet for fat loss and metabolic health. The longest trial ever run says it's not better than just eating less.
- [Your Rest Timer Is Probably Wrong](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-rest-periods-matter.html) (2026-04-15): Most fitness apps default to 60-90 seconds between sets. The research says that's too short for trained lifters. Here's what the evidence actually shows.
- [Why Your Volume Tracking Is Lying to You](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-volume-counting-matters.html) (2026-04-08): Most fitness apps either ignore secondary muscle work or count it the same as direct work. Both are wrong. Here's the evidence-based middle ground.
- [Why Your Workout Plan Should Tell You When to Push](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-rir-matters.html) (2026-04-01): Most fitness apps give you sets and reps but never tell you how hard to actually train. The research is clear: proximity to failure is the variable that drives muscle growth.
- [Coast vs MyFitnessPal vs MacroFactor vs Hevy](https://getcoast.fit/blog/json-fit-vs-competitors.html) (2026-03-25): An honest comparison of what each app does well, where it falls short, and where Coast fits in.
- [Why You Don't Need Another AI Subscription for Fitness](https://getcoast.fit/blog/why-no-ai-subscription.html) (2026-03-19): You're already paying for ChatGPT or Claude. Why are fitness apps charging you again for the same thing?
- [How to Create a Personalised Meal Plan with Claude](https://getcoast.fit/blog/meal-plan-claude.html) (2026-03-14): Optional: have your own AI write a custom meal plan and import it into Coast for the grocery list and meal prep. The app does this itself now; this is for people who want their own AI involved.
- [How to Generate a 12-Week Hypertrophy Program with ChatGPT](https://getcoast.fit/blog/chatgpt-hypertrophy-program.html) (2026-03-08): A step-by-step tutorial walking through the full workflow, from setup to AI prompt to imported program, ready to track.

## Training programs

- [Ryan's Program](https://getcoast.fit/programs/?program=ryans-program): Upper / Lower, 4 days a week, 52 weeks. Advanced, full gym. Program file: https://getcoast.fit/programs/ryans-program.json
- [Beginner Foundation](https://getcoast.fit/programs/?program=upper-lower-beginner): Upper / Lower, 4 days a week, 52 weeks. Beginner. Program file: https://getcoast.fit/programs/upper-lower-beginner.json
- [Intermediate Hybrid](https://getcoast.fit/programs/?program=ppl-upper-lower): Push / Pull / Legs plus Upper / Lower, 5 days a week, 54 weeks. Intermediate. Program file: https://getcoast.fit/programs/ppl-upper-lower.json
- [Advanced High-Volume](https://getcoast.fit/programs/?program=ppl-advanced): Push / Pull / Legs twice, 6 days a week, 52 weeks. Advanced. Program file: https://getcoast.fit/programs/ppl-advanced.json
